clue.text: Jacket carrying or concealing arms

definitions.meaning: a short sleeveless coat, as once worn by knights and now by heralds
the garment either displays a coat of arms or covers the armour worn beneath it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' works twice: heraldic arms embroidered on the coat, or the armour it hides.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald's sleeveless coat bears the royal arms, and a knight's version was worn over his armour.

clue.text: Character of island chief

parts.note: an ait is a small river island, as on the Thames

explanation.surface: The personality of the leader of an island community.
explanation.definitionFit: The spelt-out name of a letter of the alphabet, a written character.

clue.text: Stucco is a material for sound properties

indicators.note: material is read as made of these letters, which are reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: Plaster as a building material suited to good concert-hall sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' is the anagram signal: STUCCO IS A rearranges into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The way a room carries and reflects noise, as in a concert hall.

clue.text: Evergreen author in untidy den

indicators.note: in means the writer's initials sit inside the jumbled den
untidy means the letters of den are messed up

parts.note: APH was the familiar signature of A. P. Herbert, humorist and MP

explanation.surface: An evergreen novelist working in a messy study.
explanation.walkthrough: A. P. Herbert, the British humorist and MP, signed himself with his initials. 'untidy' scrambles the den and 'in' puts the author inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant flowering shrub, many species of which keep their leaves all year.

clue.text: Humbug to make mouth water effect slight

parts.note: humbug is a swindle or fraud, a con
to make someone's mouth water is to tempt them

explanation.surface: A boiled sweet so delicious it makes the mouth water, though only slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: HUMBUG is also a British striped boiled sweet, which feeds the sweet-shop surface. 'Effect' simply links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To slight someone is to treat them with disdain, so the noun slight is a show of scorn.

clue.text: Regular customer for tuck so to speak

definitions.meaning: someone who always does the same thing, a habitual patron
Friar Tuck, Robin Hood's monk, is a being in a monastic gown

explanation.walkthrough: Tuck is Friar Tuck of the Robin Hood legends; a monk's robe is a habit. 'Tuck' also means school food in Britain, hence 'customer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person stuck in routine, and punningly a friar dressed in his order's robe.

clue.text: Rocks on the point are superfluous

parts.note: the Needles are chalk stacks off the Isle of Wight
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Rocks standing on a headland serve no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: THE NEEDLES are a row of chalk sea stacks off England's Isle of Wight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unnecessary is surplus to requirements.

clue.text: Being at home is attractive

parts.note: an elf is a supernatural being
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone who finds staying in the house appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Small and delicately charming, like a fairy creature.

clue.text: Limit Cupid in art works, being strait-laced

indicators.note: works means the letters are worked into a new arrangement
limit means Cupid is cut short, losing its end letter

explanation.surface: Restricting depictions of a naked Cupid in artworks is prudish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limit' trims CUPID to CUPI; 'works' rearranges CUPI with IN ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Severely strict in morals, like the seventeenth-century Protestant reformers.

clue.text: Heavens! Tom rolls into a ball

indicators.note: into means the scrambled Tom goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a ball is a sphere

indicators.note: rolls suggests the three letters of Tom tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A cry of surprise as Tom, perhaps a cat, curls up into a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavens!' looks like an exclamation but is the definition. 'rolls' scrambles Tom and 'into' sets it inside the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The heavens can mean the sky, the air surrounding the earth.

clue.text: Trading station just short of river

indicators.note: just short of means the river's name falls one letter short, losing its end

parts.note: the Forth is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: A trading post sited a little way before you reach the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The FORTH is the river flowing into the Firth of Forth past Edinburgh; drop its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fur-trading posts in Canada, like those of the Hudson's Bay Company, were called forts.

clue.text: Trunk and fruit of a tree

parts.note: a trunk is a large box for storage, a chest
a nut is a hard-shelled fruit

explanation.surface: A botany lesson on the stem and seeds of some tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' pretends to be the stem of the tree, but it is the luggage sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse or sweet variety is a large deciduous tree of the beech family.

clue.text: Unit of measurement for an animal's lead of course

definitions.meaning: a measure of extent, such as the span of a swimming pool
the margin by which a horse leads on a racecourse, one body's extent

explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads like 'naturally' but means 'on the racecourse'.
explanation.definitionFit: A racehorse wins by so many body-measures, and the word also names any extent in space.

clue.text: Income tax item needs this form of conveyance

indicators.note: read as 'in come', telling the solver the answer comes in the next words

explanation.surface: A tax return item claiming the cost of a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'tax item'; 'Income' split as 'in come' points to it, and 'needs this' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired cab is a means of getting about town.

clue.text: "And smooth as monumental " (Othello)

parts.note: fill the gap in Othello's line about Desdemona's skin, smooth as the white stone of tomb effigies

explanation.walkthrough: Othello, before killing Desdemona, speaks of her skin 'whiter than snow, And smooth as monumental' stone.
explanation.definitionFit: The white translucent stone used for funeral effigies completes Shakespeare's line.

clue.text: Colour of two flowers

parts.note: a rose is one flower
a pink is another, a dianthus

explanation.surface: A shade named after a couple of blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale reddish shade used to describe fabrics and paint.

clue.text: No light reason for not playing

definitions.meaning: a sports field too dim for play to continue

explanation.definitionFit: Utterly black, and, punningly, gloom on the field that stops a game.

clue.text: Happening before the good King looked out

definitions.text: Happening before the good King looked out

parts.words: Happening before the good King looked out
parts.note: the carol says Good King Wenceslas looked out when the snow lay round about, so something had already come down

explanation.walkthrough: The Christmas carol 'Good King Wenceslas' has him look out 'when the snow lay round about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A coming-down of flakes from the sky, which must precede snow lying on the ground.

clue.text: He chose a bride from an original portrait right away

definitions.text: He chose a bride from an original portrait right away

parts.words: He chose a bride from an original portrait right away
parts.note: in The Merchant of Venice a suitor picks the lead casket holding Portia's likeness; 'original portrait right away' also hints at PORTRAIT losing R and T and being rearranged to give her name

explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's suitor chose among gold, silver and lead caskets; the lead one held Portia's picture, winning her hand at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shakespearean suitor who wins Portia of Belmont by choosing the casket with her painting.

clue.text: Instant approval

definitions.meaning: a moment, as in 'just a second'
a mark on a page showing something is correct

explanation.definitionFit: Both a brief moment, as in 'wait a sec', and a check mark signalling assent.

clue.text: Got through the ticket man

parts.note: a pass is a ticket of admission
Ed is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man who checks tickets lets someone pass.
explanation.definitionFit: Succeeded in an exam, or made it past a barrier.

clue.text: Cut includes everyone in the plant

indicators.note: includes means the word for cut holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: to cut grass is to mow it
everyone is all

explanation.surface: A trim that takes in every specimen in the plant nursery.
explanation.definitionFit: A pink-flowered herb, related to hollyhocks, that grows in hedgerows.

clue.text: Inexorable force shown by one in record century

indicators.note: in means the numeral goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a log is a record, as kept on a ship
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Unstoppable power shown by the top player in the record books over a hundred years.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning that compels assent, as in 'the inescapable force of the argument'.

clue.text: Erica's informed about an article

indicators.note: about means the word for informed goes round the article

parts.note: to be informed of news is to hear it
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A woman named Erica has been told about some newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: Erica is the botanical genus of these moorland shrubs; the possessive must be read as a plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the Latin genus name for the moorland shrubs of the heath family.

clue.text: A Hornblower female?

indicators.note: blower, split off the end of Hornblower, means the letters before it are blown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking whether there is a woman in C. S. Forester's Hornblower naval novels.
explanation.walkthrough: Hornblower is C. S. Forester's naval hero; here the word splits into A HORN as fodder and 'blower' as the instruction to scatter it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish girl's name, so a woman, as the question mark signals.

clue.text: Kind of party to follow

definitions.meaning: an all-male celebration before a wedding
an old sense of the verb: to watch or shadow someone

explanation.definitionFit: A men-only night out before a wedding, and a dated verb meaning to dog someone's steps.

clue.text: Initially he just fails to make the Theatre

definitions.meaning: the initials HE stand for His Excellency, the title of an envoy

definitions.text: just fails to make the Theatre
definitions.meaning: a London West End theatre; one letter short of its name

explanation.walkthrough: The Ambassadors Theatre is in London's West End; the singular falls an S short. 'Initially he' means the letters H.E.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy is styled His Excellency, and he is one letter short of a famous London playhouse.

clue.text: Ornamental handcuff

definitions.meaning: an ornament worn round the wrist
slang for a manacle, usually in the plural

explanation.definitionFit: A decorative band for the wrist, and criminal slang for manacles.

clue.text: Harsh terms for glove-maker turning to make lace

indicators.note: turning means the material for gloves is read backwards

parts.note: kid, young goatskin, is the leather that fine gloves are made from
to tat is to make lace by hand

explanation.surface: A glovemaker forced by harsh terms to switch trades to lace-making.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree imposed by a ruler without consultation, setting strict conditions.
